title: Network Reconnaissance
instructions: A suspicious device is on the tournament network. Use the reconnaissance tools in the Evidence panel to identify the open ports and the rogue host.

messages.text: An unknown device sits on the tournament network. Open the case file and map it before anyone acts.

notify.text: Map the host before you touch it - the scan tells you what it reaches.
notify.speaker: instructor

notify.text: Watch what talks outbound. Beacon intervals give implants away.
notify.speaker: instructor

briefing.narrative: The tournament's network operations center has detected an unknown device. Before any action is taken, you must map the network: identify which ports are open on the target and find the rogue host. Open the evidence as needed, then make your calls.
briefing.speaker: instructor

recon.narrative: You have an nmap scan of the 192.168.1.0/24 subnet. Review the scan results in the Evidence panel and identify which ports are actually open on the target device.
recon.speaker: instructor

choices.feedback: Correct. Only those three ports are in the open state.

choices.text: All discovered ports are suspicious and should be flagged
choices.feedback: Too broad. Port 8080 is closed, and open services alone are not proof of compromise.

host_analysis.narrative: Now that you know the open ports, examine the host inventory and the packet capture to identify which host is unauthorized and communicating with an external IP.
host_analysis.speaker: instructor

choices.feedback: Correct. It is the only host not in the authorized inventory and it shows external traffic.
The stream box is listed as authorized. The rogue device is .105.

complete.narrative: Reconnaissance complete. The target's open services and the rogue host have been identified. This information feeds into the vulnerability disclosure phase.
complete.speaker: instructor
